results.content:
with 0 comments

Developers using GitHub Copilot have access to several AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. While having multiple models provides flexibility, devs often need to manually select the right model for each task. At GitHub Universe 2026, GitHub announced a new feature called GitHub Copilot Fusion, which automatically selects and combines AI models to complete coding tasks.

Screenshot of GitHub Copilot Fusion in the GitHub interface with a dark theme A dropdown menu labele

Copilot Fusion combines GitHub's existing automatic model selection technology with the multi-model orchestration capabilities of Project HydraFusion, which was introduced as a research preview in September. [...] Instead of selecting a specific AI model, devs can now select Copilot Fusion from the model picker. Based on the complexity of the task, Copilot Fusion automatically decides which models to use and whether multiple models need to work together.

GitHub has introduced three effort levels for Copilot Fusion:

 Fusion Standard: Prioritizes efficiency and cost for everyday coding tasks.
 Fusion High: Uses more capable models and additional reasoning for complex coding tasks.
 Fusion Max: Prioritizes the most capable models for demanding tasks that require deeper reasoning.

Depending on the selected effort level and the task, Copilot Fusion can use three different execution patterns: [...] Single: One AI model completes the task directly.
 Cascade: A cost-efficient model first attempts the task. Another model evaluates the result and decides whether a more capable model should take over.
 Critique: One model generates a response, while other models review it and provide feedback. The original model then revises its response.

The interesting part is that developers don't need to manage the above workflows. Copilot Fusion automatically decides when additional model calls are necessary, helping avoid unnecessary costs and delays for simpler tasks.

GitHub has made Copilot Fusion generally available, turning the experimental multi-model orchestration it had been testing under the name HydraFusion into a standard option in the Copilot model picker. Announced on October 28, 2026 in the GitHub changelog and in the company's GitHub Universe 2026 keynote post, Fusion changes the basic question developers answer before every Copilot request. Instead of choosing a specific model, the user chooses Copilot Fusion and an effort level, and Copilot decides which model or combination of models handles the task, how they are chained together and how much reasoning each step receives. [...] According to GitHub, Fusion is available on all Copilot plans and works in Visual Studio Code, the GitHub Copilot app, GitHub Copilot CLI and JetBrains IDEs, with support for other clients described as coming soon. It combines two strands of earlier work: the multi-model orchestration developed in the Project HydraFusion research preview and the fine-tuned model selection that powered Copilot's auto model selection. In JetBrains IDEs, GitHub says Fusion replaces the existing Auto model option and is rolling out gradually to all users.

# Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion

A GitHub Copilot prompt composer with the Copilot Fusion settings menu open. Fusion is enabled, and the effort-level options are Standard, High, and Max; Max is selected.

GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.

Copilot Fusion brings together Project HydraFusion’s multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection’s fine-tuned model selection, leveraging the benefits of both to balance performance and cost efficiency. [...] Since Project HydraFusion launched, we’ve improved its performance. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. It delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task.

## Smarter choices for developers

When you select Copilot Fusion in the model picker, you aren’t selecting a specific model. You’re choosing a system that routes and orchestrates models for each task. There’s no need to switch models during a task or decide which model suits each step. For each prompt, Copilot Fusion determines which models to use and how they work together, while you choose the right level of effort. [...] To use it, select Copilot Fusion in the model picker, then choose the effort level.

 Fusion Standard: Prioritizes versatile models for everyday coding.
 Fusion High: Prioritizes capable models for challenging tasks and deeper reasoning.
 Fusion Max: Prioritizes the most capable models for the most demanding tasks and complex reasoning.

Watch as Copilot Fusion analyzes each task and selects a model to complete it, orchestrating multiple models through the following workflows when needed.

 Single: One model solves the task directly.
 Cascade: An efficient model drafts a response. A quality check determines whether to accept it or escalate to a stronger model.
 Critique: One model drafts an initial response, another model reviews it, and the original model revises.
